findings.reason: The action uses the default Node HTTP/1 adapter; httpVersion:2 is never enabled.
Only the fixed official public-DNS HTTPS connector is used, not internal IP targets whose CIDR NO_PROXY exclusion would be security-critical.
The Node HTTP adapter is used; the affected fetch adapter is not selected.
The action uses the default Node HTTP/1 adapter; httpVersion:2 is never enabled.
All requests use explicit get/post method aliases, which are unaffected by the default-instance inherited-method path.
All requests use fixed official HTTPS connector routes; no data: URL is accepted.
The logging interceptor returns the original null-prototype config including its own headers; it never replaces config with a minimal plain object.

The socket-hijack gadget requires prior same-process Object.prototype pollution; the pinned action has no untrusted config/object merge or prototype-pollution source. Fixed HTTPS routes remain mandatory.

The connector URL and route construction are fixed to the official trusted HTTPS service; untrusted origins or redirect Locations are not accepted as inputs. Availability remains dependent on that service.
